question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund received unlisted shares as part of a distressed-arb deal at INR 40 lakh where FMV per prescribed rules was INR 60 lakh. Under Section 56(2)(x) (deemed income from inadequate consideration) and the workbook's effective rate of 34.944% for 'other investors', the tax impact on the deemed income is:

answer.text: Nil — Section 56(2)(x) does not apply to AIFs
INR 6,98,880 (34.944% on the shortfall of INR 20 lakh)

explanation.text: The Logic: Shortfall = FMV 60L − consideration 40L = INR 20L, exceeds the INR 0.05 million (INR 50,000) threshold in Section 56(2)(x). Fund is an 'other investor' (trust); effective tax rate per workbook table = 34.944%. Tax = 20,00,000 × 34.944% = INR 6,98,880. The Trap: A is false — Section 56(2)(x) applies to any acquirer. C uses the individual/HUF rate (42.744%) rather than the trust/other rate (34.944%). D uses a fictional 10% rate. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B test 56(2)(x) at individual level. XIX-E tests it at fund level — if a Cat III AIF receives shares at a bargain, the shortfall is taxable as Income from Other Sources. Manager's Pro-Tip: In distressed-arb or private-placement deals where Vindhya buys below FMV, get a Cat 1 merchant banker / Rule 11UA valuation BEFORE closing. Contemporaneous valuation documentation shuts down Section 56(2)(x) reclassifications during tax audit.
